chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man forgot the Qunut, so he remembered it while he was in one of the parts of the prayer path (sequence). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should face the Qiblah, then let him say it.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'I dislike for the man that he should turn away from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) or leave it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets Qunut during prayer and remembers it later?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of reciting Qunut late in the prayer sequence if forgotten, emphasizing the Imam's preference for maintaining the Prophet's Sunnah over strict adherence to timing. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that Qunut is a highly recommended act (Sunnah) rather than an obligatory pillar, allowing for flexibility without invalidating the prayer. The Imam’s personal dislike for abandoning it underscores its spiritual significance in daily worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,
‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘A man forgets the Qunut, so he remembers it while he is in one of the roads’. So heasws said: ‘He should face towards the Qiblah, then let him say it’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> used to dislike it for the man that he should turn away from a Sunnah of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, or he leaves it’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following:
“I asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who has forgotten al-Qunut then remembers somewhere on the way. The Imam said, ‘He should turn toward Qiblah and say it.’
He then said, ‘I do not like a man’s ignoring traditions of the Messenger of Allah or abandoning them altogether.’”
